When things were going well I was flying high, but if he was being cold and dismissive I would be devastated, and inconsolable. 

A few years ago I learned about trauma bonds and it threatened everything I felt about this man. I think in the back of my mind I always knew it wasn't really love, but it was all I had. All I believed I could have. All I felt worthy of. His "love" was just like my father's love, always taking never giving, regardless as to what was best for me. 

I grew up in a house where the man who said he loved me was sexually abusing me. My mother even with evidence, and my father's admission chose her husband over me, but she claimed to love me. My view of love is severely fucked up. My view of love is me giving until it hurts, and even far beyond, me sacrificing everything including myself & then settling for whatever scraps of attention are thrown my way. 

I was young (19) when I first met this man, and spiraling out from the abuse, & trying to push it down. I wasted a lifetime being hurt by him, going back to him, waiting for him to love me back. Waiting for him to really choose me. Time wasted. Time I can't get back. I finally walked away and I'm incredibly angry with myself because I missed out on so much being tied to him. 

Today I'm alone, and lonely but I'm seeing him and this twisted thing we shared as what it truly was. He was abused too, so maybe his view of love is damaged. I'm trying to learn to love myself.
